$comment: The release security gate's invariant registry. A security rule with no test is not a rule: tests/security-registry.test.ts checks this file; scripts/release-invariants.mjs runs the installed-package tests. Design: the release security gate (R1, 2026-10-07; build plan ruled 2026-10-13).

invariants.statement: No token is issued over HTTP (register, pair, recovery or any HTTP path) without a credential bound to the row or the mint secret. stdio is OUT of scope per PR-D Q6, CONDITIONAL on SEC-04 holding (a stdio register is a same-user act gated by DB-file access).
invariants.source: ADR-0009, ADR-0006, PR-D Q1/Q-A/Q6; ruled 13 Oct

tests/release/sec-01.release.ts::SEC-01.T1 BOUNDARY stdio (PR-D Q6): a NEW name over stdio registers WITHOUT a secret, as ruled
tests/release/sec-01.release.ts::SEC-01.T1 TWIN http: the same register WITH the registration secret issues a token
tests/release/sec-01.release.ts::SEC-01.T1 TWIN http: an existing name refreshes itself with its own token, no secret

invariants.statement: No secret or token appears in any argv, stdout/stderr (except an explicit flagged output), logs, /health or error text.

The private chain (instance dir, secrets dir, secret file, relay.db and its -wal/-shm) is owner-only by ownership AND mode/ACL; otherwise mint is unavailable. LOAD-BEARING: SEC-01's stdio exclusion holds only while this does.

invariants.statement: B never decides; no A write outside a unit; no external I/O without a committed effect row; a revoked origin's effects are withheld; child authority only via activation.

Every token consumer refuses a token whose row is not authorized by auth_state (revoked, recovery_pending, provisioning), never the hash alone; a revoked row becomes active only via relay recover, a recovery_pending row only via its own recovery token or relay recover.

invariants.statement: Every security- or liveness-relevant subprocess runs by an ABSOLUTE trusted path, never one found through PATH. Windows: whoami, icacls, reg and powershell come from a validated %SystemRoot%; a missing or invalid SystemRoot is a named error that fails closed, never a PATH fallback. A new by-name subprocess in src/ fails CI unless it is allowlisted with its reason.
invariants.source: #336 (d504c4d); this gate's first catch (windows-2022, 13 Oct); Codex #336 R1, R2
